findings.evidence: "MEASURED — an instrumented run under the Chapter 14 protocol; used only where the book reports a benchmark it actually ran, never for a planning screen. ANALYTICAL — arithmetic on stated inputs … HYPOTHESIS — reasoned but not yet validated … ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example … The four registers above are not one axis: MEASURED, ANALYTICAL and HYPOTHESIS name what was done to a number, whereas [ILLUSTRATIVE] names where it came from — so a single claim can be both ILLUSTRATIVE and ANALYTICAL."
findings.issue: Internal contradiction in the evidence-panel definition. The panel opens by presenting 'four registers' as a unified set, then states 'The four registers above are not one axis' — denying they form one axis while having just framed them as four parallel registers. Worse, MEASURED is listed as a register in this panel, but the Preface axis note (p.19) says 'measurement status therefore uses ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED or UNMEASURED' — i.e., MEASURED is a measurement-status value on Axis 3, not a register (the registers are Axis 1 provenance + Axis 2 epistemic status). The panel never reconciles MEASURED's dual role. Separately, ANALYTICAL appears both as one of the four 'registers' and as a measurement status on Axis 3, with no statement of whether these are the same item or two uses of one word. A reader cannot tell from this panel alone how to apply the labels correctly.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the evidence-panel opening to state plainly that two label axes (provenance, epistemic status) plus an optional measurement-status axis are used, drop the 'four registers' framing (or define exactly which axis each of the four belongs to), and add one sentence clarifying whether MEASURED and ANALYTICAL as used in the panel are the same items as the Axis-3 measurement statuses or distinct categories.

findings.evidence: Figure 1 caption: "Two loops are drawn: the inner (green, left) returns a failed benchmark or TCO validation from 'Validate & Defend' to 'Design & size'; the outer (red, right) returns from 'Commit' to 'Understand' when a requirements revision is needed." In-figure text (rendered page): "iterate", "re-derive" appear as edge labels; stage category labels "understand / define / size / justify / decide" also appear in the figure.
findings.issue: Two defects in one caption. (1) The caption identifies the two loops only by color ('green', 'red') and position ('left', 'right'), but the book's own stated convention (Ch. 7 intro, p.143: 'Color is not semantic anywhere in this chapter's figures'; and the general figure convention, p.42: 'Color is figure-local decoration') warns readers not to rely on color — in a grayscale print or photocopy the two loops become indistinguishable. (2) The caption does not mention the in-figure edge labels 'iterate' and 're-derive' or the four stage-category labels (understand, define, size, justify, decide) that appear in the figure, so the caption under-describes what the figure shows and a reader cannot tell from the caption alone what those words mean.
findings.fix_instruction: Identify the loops by their edge labels and stage endpoints (e.g., 'the inner loop, labelled iterate …; the outer loop, labelled re-derive …') rather than by color/position alone, and add one clause naming the stage-category labels visible in the figure.

findings.evidence: Page 16 register definition: "ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED), on the book's teaching geometry". Page 17: "[ILLUSTRATIVE] is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical worked example... [canonical scenario]/[ILLUSTRATIVE] says whether it is the book's fixed reference set or a one-off what-if." and "A vendor hardware constant (e.g. the H100 footprint) is [1P][FACT], never [ILLUSTRATIVE]."
findings.issue: The same named register/tag has two contradictory scopes two pages apart: on p. xii the ILLUSTRATIVE register explicitly includes "[canonical scenario]" inputs, while p. xiii defines the [ILLUSTRATIVE] tag as reserved for non-canonical examples and distinct from [canonical scenario]. A reader cannot tell from p. xii whether a canonical-scenario number belongs inside the ILLUSTRATIVE register.
findings.fix_instruction: Restrict the p. xii register parenthetical to "([ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED)" and describe canonical-scenario inputs in their own register, or explicitly state that the register name and the Axis-1 tag differ in scope.

findings.evidence: PDF p. 16: "ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED), on the book’s teaching geometry, to be re-derived per deployment; this is a provenance tag (Axis 1) only, not a measurement status"; same page: "Axis note: [ILLUSTRATIVE] is a provenance tag (Axis 1) only — a non-canonical worked example — and is never a measurement status".
findings.issue: The evidence taxonomy contradicts itself inside the same paragraph. ILLUSTRATIVE is first defined as including [canonical scenario] and as being on the book’s teaching geometry, but the Axis note immediately says ILLUSTRATIVE is non-canonical. This can cause load-bearing labels to be read under the wrong provenance rule.
findings.fix_instruction: Remove [canonical scenario] from the ILLUSTRATIVE definition and remove 'on the book’s teaching geometry' as a defining condition. State that [canonical scenario] and [ILLUSTRATIVE] are distinct Axis-1 provenances and that ILLUSTRATIVE covers non-canonical worked examples only.
